correctness.rationale: The initial q-clique-free complex of two large plus s singleton shores strong-collapses to the (q−2)-skeleton of the simplex on s+2 shores, with top integral rank C(s+1,q−1)=h+d. Any face newly allowed after deleting matched edge a_i b_i must meet exactly q shores and consist of those two endpoints and exactly q−2 singleton vertices; therefore each stage attaches precisely d (q−1)-simplices whose boundaries lie in X0. Under the strong-collapse shore map, each attaching sphere maps to a boundary ∂[A,B,S] in the standard integral basis ∂[A,T], selecting a primitive rank-d direct summand, independent of i. For q>=4 the (q−2)-sphere wedge is simply connected and Hurewicz identifies π_{q−2} and H_{q−2}. First attachment kills d summands; every later attaching class becomes nullhomotopic and wedges d S^{q−1}, giving h permanent low-dimensional classes, initial d low classes dying at stage 1, and later split high-degree births, all torsion-free. Independent graph-subset/finite GF2 homology and face-difference checks in q=4,5 matched families agreed; integral all-parameter conclusion rests on the primitive attaching-basis proof.
